one_liner: SIMD C CSV parser/CLI beating DuckDB and Polars on read throughput, with a slow correct fallback for nonstandard quoting.
what_it_does: zsvlib is a C library plus `zsv` CLI for parsing, re-emitting, and querying CSV, generic-delimited, and fixed-width tabular data, exposing row- and cell-level push/pull APIs built around zsv_new/zsv_parse_more/zsv_finish/zsv_delete and row_handler/cell_handler callbacks. It is not a drop-in for any existing library's API; callers write handler callbacks and drive the parse loop, or use the CLI subcommands (`count`, `select`, `sql`, `2json`, etc.) directly. By default it handles real-world 'dirty' CSV the way Excel does (embedded newlines, ragged rows, unescaped mid-cell quotes), and the CLI is extensible via plugin shared libraries.
how_it_is_fast: The default 'compat' parser is a byte-by-byte state machine; the optional `--parser fast` mode adds a SIMD path using branchless prefix-XOR carry propagation to track quote state across a buffer, available on aarch64 (NEON) and x86-64 (AVX2, SSE2). Either parser mode can be combined with `--parallel` to split input across threads/cores. The library also targets a small, roughly input-size-independent memory footprint rather than buffering whole rows or tables.
when_to_use: Bulk row counting or column-selection/re-shaping over large CSVs (hundreds of MB+) where wall-clock throughput matters more than a dataframe API
CSV known or verified to be RFC-4180-compliant, so `zsv fast --parallel` can be used safely
Memory-constrained environments (embedded, containers, CI) — zsv's own README claims ~1.5MB single-threaded footprint vs 76MB (DuckDB) and 475MB (Polars) on the same task
Need a small embeddable C library or a WebAssembly build rather than a full dataframe/query engine
Need default handling of 'dirty' real-world CSV (stray unescaped quotes, ragged row lengths) without extra configuration
when_not_to_use: Input has nonstandard (non-RFC-4180) quoting and you want the fastest path — `zsv fast`, alone or with `--parallel`, produces incorrect output on such data per zsv's own benchmark page; must fall back to the slower `compat` parser
You need SQL/dataframe operations, joins, or broader analytics — DuckDB and Polars are full engines, zsv's `sql` command is CSV-file-scoped
Workload is `select`-style full-parse-plus-output on unquoted or sparsely-quoted data — sibling `xan`, single-threaded, beats single-threaded zsv there on zsv's own results page

You need documented thread-safety for sharing one parser instance across threads; not stated in the API header — `--parallel` in the CLI partitions the file rather than exposing a safe shared-parser contract
Non-C/C++ stack without willingness to wrap the C API or shell out to the CLI — only a community-maintained Ruby binding exists

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (source-drop also possible; `./configure && make install` builds both; CLI extensions are plugin shared libraries)
integration.dependencies: none documented for the core parser/library; some CLI subcommands (`sql`, `jq`, `sheet`) bundle their own dependencies, not itemized in the README
integration.min_toolchain: C, unspecified standard; GCC 11+ recommended (clang also supported), plus a basic unix toolchain (sh, make/gmake)
integration.platforms: macOS (clang/gcc), Linux (gcc), Windows (mingw64), BSD (gcc), and WebAssembly (emscripten); the SIMD fast parser additionally needs aarch64 NEON or x86-64 AVX2/SSE2, other targets use the scalar compat parser
integration.thread_safety: not documented for a single zsv_parser instance shared across threads; `--parallel` in the CLI internally partitions the input across separate parser instances rather than one instance being called concurrently
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — callback-driven C API and a separate CLI, not source- or API-compatible with DuckDB, Polars, or any existing CSV library

gotchas: `zsv fast`, with or without `--parallel`, gives incorrect output on non-RFC-4180 quoting (confirmed 'incorrect' on the nonstandard_quoted row of zsv's own results page); use `compat` for untrusted or dirty CSV

DuckDB and Polars in zsv's benchmark were run with relaxed quote/newline handling ('handicaps' per app/benchmark/README.md) to be competitive, so the headline speedups overstate the gap at correctness-equivalent settings
The much-cited memory numbers (1.5MB vs 76MB/475MB) come from a separate 433MB worldcitiespop run described in app/benchmark/README.md, not from the quoting benchmark page
A use-after-free bug was found via ASan and fixed (issue #605, closed) — the project runs ASan in CI, but this indicates memory-safety has needed active fixing, not just inspection-level trust
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick zsv over xan/DuckDB/Polars when you want a small embeddable C library (or WASM target) rather than a broader dataframe/query engine, or specifically need row counting, where zsv wins across all quoting types on its own benchmark; pick xan instead for `select`-style full-parse-and-output on unquoted or sparsely-quoted data, where single-threaded xan beats single-threaded zsv on zsv's own results page.
verified_claims_summary: On zsv's first-party darwin-arm64 (Apple M3 Pro) results page, `zsv fast --parallel` counted rows on a 500,000x20 unquoted CSV in 0.008s (14.29 GB/s) versus 0.085s for multi-threaded DuckDB v0.10.2 (default settings), 0.049s for DuckDB with quote recognition disabled, and 0.092s for single-threaded Python Polars 1.35.2; the zsv binary's compiler and optimization flags are not stated on the page.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-23, CI-gated) and MIT-licensed, so it's reasonable to depend on directly rather than vendor, though it has a small following (397 stars) and a small maintainer base.
